How it works in New York City

The rules, in plain words.

How does alternate side parking work in New York City?

Alternate side parking: no parking on the side of the street and at the hours the broom sign shows, Monday to Saturday, all year, so the sweeper can pass.

When does it apply?

All year, Monday to Saturday. A $65 ticket, no tow. No ASP on the City's suspension days (holidays, and some snow days).

What does a ticket cost?

A ticket is $65, with no tow. The City's page ↗

Can CURB remind me?

Yes. Tap your curb on the map, then Sweep alerts: a push the evening before and 30 minutes before it starts, on New York City time, or put it in your calendar. An overnight sweep gets one alert around 9 PM the evening before. On iPhone, add the map to your Home Screen first.

Is CURB free?

Yes. Free, with no account and no ads, and open source on GitHub. CURB started in San Francisco; the New York City map is built on the City's open data.

The receipts

Where the data comes from

The rules are the broom signs in NYC DOT's sign inventory (Parking Regulation Locations and Signs), read from their text. Each sign order names its street, cross streets and side; CURB walks the City's street centerlines (CSCL) between the two cross streets, guided by the signs' own points, and puts the rule on that side. ASP is also suspended for snow and emergencies, announced the same day by 311 and Notify NYC. The posted sign always wins: temporary signs and holidays override everything here.
